info.title: Nomadu agent API
info.summary: A traveller's timeline, visa and tax standing, and plans, for an AI agent acting on their behalf.
info.description:
Nomadu tracks where its user is, day by day, and works out visa allowances and tax residency from that. This API gives an agent the same data and numbers the app shows, plus the ability to plan trips and, when the user allows it, to correct the timeline.

## Authentication
Every request except this spec and `/docs` needs `Authorization: Bearer nmd_…`. The user creates the token in the app (Settings, AI agent) and decides at that moment whether the token may edit the timeline. A token that may not gets `403 forbidden` on `POST /trips`, `PATCH /trips/{id}` and `DELETE /trips/{id}`; everything else works for every token. A revoked token answers `401`.

## Conventions
All bodies are JSON. Dates are calendar days as `YYYY-MM-DD` in the user's local reckoning; there are no times. Days are counted inclusively: a stay from the 1st to the 3rd is 3 days. Countries can be given by English name or by ISO code; unknown countries are rejected, not guessed. Errors are `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`.

## Two kinds of travel
**Stays** (`/trips`) are the past: where the user actually was, recorded by the phone. **Journeys** (`/journeys`) are plans: a title and a chain of stops with dates. A stay cannot start in the future and a plan is never counted as presence. When the user says "I am going to Hanoi next month", that is a journey; "I was in Hanoi last month and the app missed it", that is a stay.

## Accommodation
Every planned stop can carry one accommodation plan (`/journeys/{id}/stops/{stopId}/accommodation`): whether a place is needed, what it should be like, the options that were found, the one that was picked and, once booked, the booking details. You research on the platforms yourself and save what you found here; Nomadu never searches or books anything. A plan is planning only: it never becomes a stay in the timeline and never changes visa or tax numbers. Check-in and check-out are stored on the plan and validated; when a stop is later moved, the plan keeps its dates and reports `dates_match_stop: false`, so ask the user before changing a booking. Every token may read and write plans, the same as journeys. `GET /accommodations?status=searching` lists the stops that still need a place; every stop in `/journeys` carries a one-line summary of its plan.

## What the app does with your writes
Everything you create or change syncs to the user's phone within seconds while the app is open, or on its next start. Tell the user when you have written something. Deleting is soft: the record is tombstoned and disappears from the app.

bearer.bearerFormat: nmd_ token from the Nomadu app

message.description: Human readable, safe to show or repeat to the user

Citizenship.description: null until the user has finished onboarding; /visa and /tax then answer 409.

Trip.description: One tracked stay in one city. The timeline is the list of these, in date order, with no gaps while tracking runs.

end_date.description: null while the stay is still going on (only the newest stay can be open)

days.description: Calendar days, first and last day both counted

StayInput.description: A past stay to add. Give the country by name or code. Both dates are required: an open stay belongs to the tracker.

country.description: Country name in English; alternative to country_code

start_date.description: First day. Cannot be in the future; future travel is a journey.

id.description: Stable across edits: reuse it by sending the same city and country in a PATCH

transport.description: How the traveller gets to this stop

accommodation.description: The stop's accommodation plan in one line, null when none has been started

StopInput.description: A planned stop. Only the first stop needs a start_date; every later stop starts the day after the previous one ends. Each stop needs either days or end_date.

country.description: Country name in English; alternative to country_code

start_date.description: Only read on the first stop (today when omitted). Later stops chain.

end_date.description: Last day of the stop, inclusive. Alternative to days.

days.description: Length of the stop. Alternative to end_date.

start_date.description: First day of the first stop

end_date.description: Last day of the last stop

VisaStatus.description: How much of a visa allowance is used. From the built-in visa rules for the citizenship, or from a visa the user entered.

usagePeriod.description: The stay or year the count belongs to

isUserVisa.description: true when the rule is a visa the user typed in

lastStayDays.description: Per-stay rules only: length of the most recent finished stay

leftOn.description: Per-stay rules only: the day that stay ended

source.description: Where the built-in rule can be checked

lastVerified.description: When the built-in rule was last audited

TaxStatus.description: Days present in a country against its tax residency threshold, counted over that country's tax year: the calendar year for most, 6 April to 5 April for GB, 1 July to 30 June for AU, the busiest 12-month window for NZ.

ruleLabel.example: 183 days in the 2026/27 tax year (Apr 6 to Apr 5)

year.description: The year asked for; which days that covers is in periodStart and periodEnd.

periodKind.description: A fixed tax year, or any window of that length (NZ).

totalCountries.description: Countries with at least one day in the window

daysAway.description: Distinct days outside the home country. The headline number.

daysInWindow.description: Days the window spans so far

newCountries.description: Countries first visited inside the window

topCountries.description: Distinct days per country, biggest first

daysAwayByMonth.description: Twelve buckets for a year, null for all time

AccommodationStatus.description: Where the plan stands. Moves forward on its own when something happens (an option is added: options_available; one is selected: selected; a booking is saved: booked) and can be set by hand any time with PUT …/status. open: nothing done yet. searching: looking for places. options_available: at least one option saved. deciding: the user is choosing. selected: one option picked, not booked. booked: booking details saved. checked_in, completed: the stay itself. cancelled: sticks until set to something else.

AccommodationRequirements.description: What the place should be like. Every field is optional; absent keeps the current value, null clears it.

budget_per_night.description: Ceiling per night. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

budget_total.description: Ceiling for the whole stay. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 for both budgets. Required when either budget is given.

areas.description: Neighbourhoods or areas to look in. Lower-cased and de-duplicated; may also be sent as one comma-separated string.

min_requirements.description: Must-haves in words: "private bathroom, no ground floor"

work_requirements.description: What working from there needs: "stable wifi 50 Mbit, quiet, a desk"

amenities.description: Wanted amenities. The app knows wifi, desk, quiet, ac, kitchen, washer, gym, pool, balcony, parking, breakfast; other words are kept as given. Lower-cased and de-duplicated; may also be sent as one comma-separated string.

dates_flexible.description: true when a day either side is fine

AccommodationOption.description: One place that was found. Prices are as seen on the platform; say when you looked (last_checked_at), they move.

check_out.description: Defaults to the plan's check_out; must be after check_in

total_price.description: For the whole stay, fees included if the platform shows it that way. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

price_per_night.description: Per night. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 for every price on this option. Required when any price is given.

fees.description: Cleaning and service fees on top, when shown separately. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

rating_scale.description: 5 for Airbnb and Google, 10 for Booking.com and Agoda. Send it with a rating above 5.

amenities.description: What the listing has. Lower-cased and de-duplicated; may also be sent as one comma-separated string.

score.description: Your own verdict, 0 to 10, one decimal

risks.description: What could go wrong: construction, far from transport, few reviews

last_checked_at.description: When the listing was last looked at

AccommodationOptionInput.description: An option to save or the fields of one to change. Only name is required on a new one; absent fields keep their value on a PATCH, null clears them. Free text must not contain payment card numbers.

check_out.description: Defaults to the plan's check_out; must be after check_in

total_price.description: For the whole stay, fees included if the platform shows it that way. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

price_per_night.description: Per night. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 for every price on this option. Required when any price is given.

fees.description: Cleaning and service fees on top, when shown separately. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

rating_scale.description: 5 for Airbnb and Google, 10 for Booking.com and Agoda. Send it with a rating above 5.

amenities.description: What the listing has. Lower-cased and de-duplicated; may also be sent as one comma-separated string.

score.description: Your own verdict, 0 to 10, one decimal

risks.description: What could go wrong: construction, far from transport, few reviews

last_checked_at.description: When the listing was last looked at

AccommodationBooking.description: What was booked, for the door and the desk. No payment details: card numbers are refused, and there is no field for a password or a login.

option_id.description: The option that was booked. Defaults to the selected option when the booking is first saved.

booking_url.description: Link to the reservation on the platform

price.description: What was actually paid or is due. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

check_in_info.description: How to get in: times, codes, where the key is

deposit.description: Security deposit. Two decimals; needs a currency beside it.

provider_contact.description: Host or reception: name, phone, messenger

review_rating.description: Your rating after the stay, 0 to 5

Accommodation.description: The accommodation plan of one stop: whether a place is needed, what it should be like, the options found, the pick and the booking. Planning only: it is never a stay in the timeline.

id.description: Same as stop_id: a stop has at most one plan

stop.description: The stop this plan belongs to, as it is now

needed.description: false when the user has a place already (friends, own flat) and wants no search

check_in.description: First night. Defaults to the stop's start_date.

check_out.description: Morning of departure. Defaults to the day after the stop's end_date, so nights equal the stop's days.

dates_match_stop.description: false when the stop was moved or resized after the plan was made. The plan keeps its own dates; tell the user rather than moving a booking.

notes.description: Notes on the plan as a whole

AccommodationInput.description: Fields of the plan to set. All optional; absent keeps, null clears. Options and booking have their own routes.

check_in.description: Must be a real day. Defaults to the stop's start_date on creation.

check_out.description: Must be after check_in. Defaults to the day after the stop's end_date on creation.

AccommodationSummary.description: A plan in one line, attached to every stop of a journey

selected.description: Name of the selected or booked option

Accommodation.summary: A plan with one option, selected, not yet booked

get.description: Citizenship and residence drive the visa and tax numbers. The counts tell you how much history there is before you ask for it.

has_fixed_residence.description: Whether the user keeps a home to return to; changes the tax rules applied

get.description: One entry per stay, oldest first. Without filters the whole history comes back; for "where was I in March" use both filters on that month.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only stays that end on or after this day (open stays always match)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only stays that start on or before this day

post.summary: Add a past stay the tracker missed
post.description: Needs a token that may edit the timeline. Confirm the exact dates with the user first: the stay changes their visa and tax counts the moment it exists. Coordinates are looked up from the city name, so use the common English name.

patch.description: Needs a token that may edit the timeline. Send only what changes: one or both dates, or the place (city with country or country_code). Days are recounted.

schema.description: A past stay to add. Give the country by name or code. Both dates are required: an open stay belongs to the tracker.

country.description: Country name in English; alternative to country_code

start_date.description: First day. Cannot be in the future; future travel is a journey.

delete.summary: Remove a stay that never happened
delete.description: Needs a token that may edit the timeline. Ask the user before deleting; there is no undo from your side.

get.description: For one calendar year, or all time without `year`. "Days away" counts distinct days outside the home country and is the number the app leads with.
For every country the user has been to: the rule that applies to their citizenship (or a visa they entered), and how much of it is used. `daysRemaining` is what "how long can I still stay" means.
Days present against each country's residency threshold, each over its own tax year (see TaxStatus). `resident` means the threshold is reached.

post.description: A title and one to sixty stops. Stops chain: give the first a start_date and every stop either days or end_date, and the dates of the rest follow. The plan appears in the app with the user as its only traveller.

patch.summary: Rename a plan or replace its stops
patch.description: Send `title`, `stops`, or both. `stops` replaces the whole list; a stop with the same city and country as before keeps its id and, with it, its accommodation plan. A stop that is dropped takes its plan with it. Ask the user before replacing stops they arranged by hand.

delete.description: Ask the user first. The accommodation plans of its stops go with it.

get.summary: Every accommodation plan, with its stop
get.description: Across all journeys, in check-in order. Plans whose stop no longer exists are left out. Start here for "which stops still need a place": filter by status.

parameters.name: stopId
parameters.description: The stop's id from the journey

get.description: 404 when nothing has been planned for this stop yet; `PUT` creates it. Notes live here too: `notes` on the plan, `requirements.notes`, and `risks` and `notes` on every option.

put.summary: Create the plan or change its requirements
put.description: Creates the plan when there is none (201) and updates it otherwise (200). Send only what you know; absent fields keep their value, null clears. Options and the booking are not touched here. Dates default from the stop; a budget needs a currency. PATCH does the same.

delete.description: Removes the plan with its options and booking from the stop. Ask the user first. For "no place needed" set `needed: false` instead.

parameters.name: stopId
parameters.description: The stop's id from the journey

post.description: Creates the plan too when there is none, so research can start before the requirements are written down. At most 30 options per stop. A plan that was open or searching becomes options_available. Prices need a currency; a rating above 5 needs rating_scale: 10. Say when you looked (last_checked_at).
